mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative as higher policy rates discount future equity cash flows.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a zero-move baseline (p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS crosses the threshold upward.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 2,000 monthly new jobs for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days, reflecting investor optimism about labor market strength.
failure_condition: In a regime with high inflation or negative GDP growth, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 1,000 units month-over-month for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive, as rising consumer demand boosts equity valuations.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during the identified demand expansion (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) by more than 5 points in a month predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days, as weak manufacturing signals economic weakness and risk aversion.
failure_condition: Over 20 days, the 5-day average forward returns are not negative (p > 0.05) when INDPRO declines sharply as predicted.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4.5% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to reduced labor market friction and improved investor sentiment.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive during the two-month UNRATE decline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE by at least 0.5 percentage points indicates mixed labor market signals, which predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days due to heightened uncertainty.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when both proxies move in the predicted direction.

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained monthly decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of at least 0.3%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to turn positive as lower inflation expectations reduce discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the CPI decline.

mechanism_narrative: When the combination of GDPC1 (GDP) and INDPRO both show double-digit growth in the same month, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to over-heating demand-supply dynamics and potential valuation inflation.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when both proxies show double-digit growth.
